smells.finding: decide_session_start is ~130 lines (scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py:1714-1845) doing five things in one body: ownership selection, the withhold decision, the blind scan, the bind-on-resume WRITE, and the resume-context rendering. The rework-1 reviewer flagged it at 105 lines and tied the flag to B4 directly; the fix for B4 made it longer, not shorter. This is not a style note on this gate -- B5, my blocker, lives exactly in the coupling between its first part (what `owned` means) and its fourth (what the scan-bind writes), and at this length nothing invites a reader to check that the guard covers every way the fourth part is reached. Extracting the bind step is the structural fix; the implementer named it as a triage candidate and I agree it is not this gate's work.

override.repo_standard: references/global-everyone.md 'one canonical path; no speculative abstraction', plus this gate's pinned constraint that scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py stays a single stdlib-only hook module (the import block is asserted byte-identical by the gate's own differential).
override.reason: decide_session_start and decide_stop both manipulate the binding store's internals more than their own state, which is textbook feature envy toward a binding module. There is no such module and the standard forbids inventing one here: a hook that must run stdlib-only from one file has nowhere to move the behaviour to. The smell is real and it is subordinated, not dismissed -- it is the same root the data-clumps flag names, and the flagged entry is where the recommendation lives.

smells.finding: `sid_bindings`, `owners` (session_view_provenance) and `own_key` (binding_key) are computed together and travel together at BOTH call sites, and `_own_entries` takes the last two as loose arguments. Because they are three loose locals rather than one value, the fix's discriminator had to be spelled as raw truthiness on one line -- `if spine is None and sid_bindings and not owned` -- where the three states that actually matter (owns nothing visible / owns something unusable / has no binding at all) have no names. B5 is the state that has no name. A small ownership view carrying those three fields, with owns_nothing_visible() and own_entries() on it, would have made the missing third case a visible gap rather than an unwritten one.

override.repo_standard: binding_key()'s documented contract -- 'the SINGLE place the composite per-agent key is composed anywhere in the codebase' -- together with references/global-everyone.md 'no speculative abstraction'.
override.reason: Binding identity is a raw string with a '#' separator and ownership is a raw string equality, which is primitive obsession by the letter. The repo has already answered it the way it means to: one composer function, one comparison function, both documented as sole authorities, so the two sides cannot drift. Introducing a BindingKey type inside a stdlib-only hook would be the speculative abstraction the standard forbids and would buy nothing the two chokepoints do not already buy.

One rule change forced prose edits in four places that each restate the same rule: the module-level section comment (~line 691), _is_own_entry's docstring, _own_entries' docstring, and the branch comment inside decide_session_start -- plus four test docstrings. That is shotgun surgery in the documentation dimension, and it is measurably costly here rather than theoretically: of the five false sentences I found, four are in three different restatements of the one rule. Each restatement is another copy that can go stale independently, and on this lane they have, at every rework.

decide_session_start's single body has now been edited three times on this one gate for three different reasons: how selection identifies an owner (rework 1), whether a withheld session may reach the writer (rework 2), and -- if B5 is fixed as I recommend -- what the writer itself may file. Three unrelated axes of change landing in one function is divergent change, and it is the same structural fact the long-method flag names from the other side.
The deepest chains are the pre-existing two-hop guarded reads (spine.get('engine_session') or {}).get('status'); the rework adds none.
The rework adds no symbol, no parameter, no extension point -- one hoisted local and one condition. map/INDEX.md's scripts entity count is unchanged at 1225, which is the mechanical confirmation.

The strongest smell in this diff. A one-line condition carries roughly thirty lines of comment arguing that it is correct, and the argument is where the defect hides: the paragraph explaining why the OWN-but-unreadable case is safely excluded ('this agent is contradicting no one', 'a spine nobody claimed') is false in a topology I reproduced through production writers. Fowler's point exactly -- prose was used to make a structure readable instead of the structure being made readable, and here the prose did not merely fail to help, it actively certified the gap. The same diff also carries a test NAME making a universal claim ('..._is_never_bound_to_its_in_tree_crews_spine') that the tree falsifies. This is the fifth recurrence of this defect on this lane and the first time it has concealed a blocker rather than merely misdescribed one.
